key_insight: A simulator-trained inverse map lets Bayesian optimization search a low-dimensional space while a geometry-aware Gaussian process kernel preserves relationships in the original parameter space.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can leverage an approximate mechanistic simulator to guide black-box optimization toward promising solutions with fewer search dimensions.
method: Train an inverse map offline from simulator parameters to predicted optimal controls.
Run online Bayesian optimization over the learned representation using a kernel aware of the original problem geometry.
Analyze approximation bias and information gain, deriving intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret under additional assumptions.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations of personalized Parkinson’s drug dosing show improved optimization performance, including under simulator misspecification.
watch_item: Restricting search to the learned representation can exclude the true optimum; theoretical guarantees require additional geometric and Gaussian process assumptions.
paper_title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
